To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) We developed a pre-clinlical model of motor neuron injury in mice that is reproducible, focal, and easily applied to rodents, 2) We used this model to show that a transient and focal loss of motor neurons results in a long-lasting functional defect in mice, 3) We showed that the injury was caused by a phosphatidylinositide 3’- kinase inhibitor, wortmanin, and that the inhibitor did not affect axon retrograde

we developed a new pre-clinical motor neuron injury model, that we characterized this new pre-clinicial motor neuron injury model using quantitative gene expression, and that the pre-clinical model can be used for quantitative studies on neural repair and regeneration.

the focal injection of a pro-apopotic drug into the sciatic nerve generates a reproducible, graded, and minimal invasive injury to motor neurons and a functional deficit that is easily measured and can be applied in small rodents to test the efficacy of therapeutic interventions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel, focal and reproducible motor neuron injury model for the study of neural repair and regeneration.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for spinal cord injury and amyotrophic lateral slerosis.
the use of a phosphatidylinositide-3-kinase inhibitor to selectively target the survival of motor neurons.
